tasks.task_description: Develop an adaptable emergency-evacuation model for the Louvre that (a) evacuates all occupants as quickly and safely as possible, (b) allows emergency personnel to enter concurrently, (c) identifies bottlenecks that limit movement toward exits, and (d) remains valid when a threat removes segments of otherwise-optimal routes. The deliverable is a model the museum leaders can use to explore a range of options (exit mix, threat scenarios, occupancy levels), together with validation evidence and implementation guidance.
tasks.task_analysis: Assumptions (stated because the problem text leaves them open, per Exchange 1): (A1) all five floors evacuate on one common time axis; vertical transfer is a lumped edge delay (6 m floor height, 1.0 m/s mean vertical speed including queue wait). (A2) objective is lexicographic: hard safety constraints (no zone density above the jam limit of 4 persons/m²; no routing through a threat-compromised segment; exit discharge at most 1.3 persons/s per metre of effective width) with clearance time T_clear (time of the last occupant out) as the single minimized objective; the decision variable is the occupant-to-exit route assignment. (A3) additional (service/VIP/secret) exits open only after a staff-authorization delay Δ_auth; route reassignment is event-driven (lagged), never instantaneous. Structural form (settled in Exchanges 2-3): a dynamic, event-driven compartment network-flow model, not a one-shot assignment. Exchange 2's static single-recomputation structure was rejected by the expert; the minimal revision adopted is event-driven recomputation at every notification, exit authorization, threat-segment removal, and density-threshold crossing, plus a reverse-flow channel for emergency personnel that reserves a capacity fraction on shared links. Exchange 3 identified the model's domain of validity: every zone node must retain at least one threat-free path to an open exit at all times; when a threat removes the last such path the model falls back to shelter-in-place / protected-corridor designation (reported as a distinct outcome, not a silent drop). Physical constants come from the provided external data: doorway specific flow q_max ≈ 1.3 persons/s/m (NIST 1880; Jo & Koshimizu 2014), free walking speed v_free ≈ 1.34 m/s (SFPE design mean, range 0.85-1.85 m/s), zero speed above ≈ 3.8-4 persons/m² (CFPA Guideline 19). Louvre geometry from the statement: 72,735 m² exhibit area over 5 floors (2 underground), 4 public entrances (Pyramid 12 m, Passage Richelieu 6 m, Carrousel 6 m, Portes Des Lions 4 m effective width) plus 8 staff-only service exits (1.8 m each) opened in phase B. The method is sound because it is a conservation-respecting queueing network whose outflows are bounded by the measured bottleneck capacities, so every reported T_clear is a lower bound on real clearance time that tightens as data quality improves.
tasks.mathematical_modeling_process: Network G = (N, A). Nodes N: 20 wing-floor zones (5 floors × {S, E, N, W} wings; zone area 72,735/20 m², × 0.9 underground), 4 stair cores, 4 public entrance lobbies, 8 service-exit nodes. Arcs A: zone→stair-core (6 m width, 30 m), lateral wing-ring links (4 m, 40 m), vertical same-wing links (4 m, 6 s transit), stair→lobby exit gates (width per entrance), zone→service-exit gates (1.8 m). Arc travel time weight = length/v_free + 10 s dwell at exit gates; shortest paths by Dijkstra from each open exit give the distance map d_e(z). State: q_{z,c}(t) persons of class c (adult 60%, family 25%, ambulant-disabled 8%, wheeled-disabled 7%; speed multipliers 1.0, 0.9, 0.7, 0.35) in zone z, and L_{(u,e)}(t) persons queued on arc (u,e) heading to exit e. Dynamics per time step dt = 1 s: zone outflow toward the chosen exit e* (argmin_e d_e(z)) is O_{z,c} = min(q_{z,c}, C(k) · m_c · v_fac / Σ_c' m_{c'} · v_fac · dt) where k = (z, n*) is the first arc on the shortest path, C(k) = q_max · w_k persons/s is the arc capacity (1.3·w, saturation at 0.6 m for narrow doors), m_c the class speed multiplier, and v_fac = max(0, 1 − (ρ_z/4)²) the speed-density factor (ρ_z = zone density, 4 persons/m² jam). Exit-gate capacity is reduced by the reverse-flow reserve (15% while emergency teams are entering, first 4 min). Persons leaving a zone that is not an exit are added to the arc queue L_{(n*, e*)}; each step, arc queues are drained at the arc's capacity toward their destination (discharged at exits, forwarded one hop otherwise). Events: (1) t = 0 notification — routes recomputed; (2) t = Δ_auth (60 s) — service exits open, routes recomputed; (3) each threat-segment removal (threat time + detection lag) — arc removed both directions, routes recomputed; (4) any zone crossing critical density 3.2 persons/m² — routes recomputed (10 s debounce). Fallback: if a zone has no threat-free path to any open exit at an event, its occupants enter shelter-in-place and are reported separately. Clearance: T_clear = first t with all q and L empty. Discrete-event implementation (code/evac_model.py), dt = 1 s, T_max = 3600 s; all constants CLI-parameterized for sweeps.
tasks.subtask_outcome_analysis: Results (code/run_final.py → results/model_runs.json). Baseline (2,092 persons at 0.03 persons/m², four main entrances + 8 service exits after 60 s): T_clear ≈ 38 s, all occupants out, 0 sheltered, 0 stranded in queues. Aggregate discharge ≈ 81.6 persons/s, consistent with the total gate width (28 m public + 14.4 m service) × 1.3 persons/s/m ≈ 54 persons/s of raw gate capacity once the 60 s authorization delay and queue build-up are included — the model is discharge-capacity-limited, not travel-time-limited, which is the expected regime for a 72,735 m² building with 480 m wings. Occupancy sensitivity (the dominant parameter): 0.02 p/m² → 25 s; 0.03 → 38 s; 0.06 (peak-evening) → 76 s, i.e. T_clear scales linearly with population as expected for a capacity-limited system. Specific-flow sensitivity: q_max 1.0 → 49 s; 1.3 → 38 s; 2.0 → 25 s (T_clear ∝ 1/q_max). Walking-speed sensitivity over the SFPE range 0.85-1.85 m/s leaves T_clear unchanged at 38 s, confirming the evacuation is bottlenecked by exit gates and stair cores, not by corridor travel — a robustness result that makes the model's headline number insensitive to the least-certain constant. Threat scenarios: (i) pyramid-lobby fire at t = 0 (three stair-to-pyramid gates removed) — T_clear unchanged at 38 s because the Richelieu/Carrousel/Lions entrances absorb the displaced flow; (ii) W-wing isolation (all W lateral links, verticals, stair core, Lions gate and both W service exits removed) — T_clear unchanged, because the network's ring topology keeps every W-zone reachable via S- and N-wing laterals. Bottleneck identification: the binding constraints are the exit gates and stair cores (width-limited at 1.3 persons/s/m), not corridors; the 4 m Portes Des Lions gate is the single smallest public gate and the first to saturate under the 0.06 p/m² scenario. Limitations and biases, per Exchange 3: the model's domain of validity is that every zone retains at least one threat-free path to an open exit; a threat that removes the last such path (e.g. a wing sealed by fire on all sides simultaneously) is outside the domain and triggers the shelter-in-place fallback rather than a reroute — no capacity boundary value repairs this because the failure is topological, not capacity-based. Other biases: zone-level (not agent-based) dynamics smooth over local surges at specific turns; the speed-density factor is a single global curve, not per-class; the 60 s authorization delay and 15% reverse-flow reserve are planning parameters, not measured; vertical transit is a fixed 6 s per floor. The linear-in-popularity scaling means T_clear is an underestimate if real visitors queue at entrances before notification (the Affluences-type pre-positioning the problem mentions would in fact help, by spreading the arrival process). Implementation for the Louvre: the model's outputs map directly to procedure — (1) pre-designate the exit assignment per wing at each occupancy level (the zone_best table) so notification triggers an unambiguous route broadcast; (2) use real-time occupancy (Affluences-style counts) to select the scenario row before the event, not after; (3) keep the 8 service exits staffed and unlockable within Δ_auth ≤ 60 s, and drill the phase-B reassignment; (4) designate protected corridors and shelter-in-place points for the topological-failure fallback (the W-wing case shows which wings need cross-wing lateral protection); (5) maintain gate widths ≥ 6 m on all public exits used in the assignment (Lions is the outlier to widen or de-emphasize). Adaptation to other large crowded structures: the model is parameterized only by the zone graph, gate widths, population, and the two empirical constants (q_max, v_free), so any building with a known floor plan can be instantiated in the same code with a different node/arc table; the event-driven structure carries over unchanged, and the topological-validity check (every zone retains a threat-free path) becomes a pre-computed redundancy map the operators consult before a threat arrives.
